headline: Approved $975,000 purchase of airplane hangar at Lawrence Municipal Airport for Greater Lawrence Technical School, 8-1.
summary: The City Council suspended its rule requiring new items go to committee first, then heard from GLTS Superintendent John Lavoie and others about buying a larger hangar at the Lawrence Municipal Airport. The Council approved the purchase for $975,000, with GLTS to repurchase it from the city within five months, contingent on a successful appraisal and Airport Commission approval.
decisions: Suspended Rule #6 to allow discussion of DOC # 003/26 at the full Council, roll call 8 YES to 1 NO (Laplante voted NO, Delrosario absent).

Approved DOC # 003/26, a motion for the City of Lawrence to purchase a hangar at Lawrence Municipal Airport for $975,000 on behalf of Greater Lawrence Technical School (GLTS), with GLTS to repurchase the hangar within five months for $975,000 plus additional holding costs, with amendments allowing the Council President to represent the Council during negotiations, making the purchase contingent on a successful appraisal at or above the purchase price, and contingent on Airport Commission approval; roll call 8 YES to 1 NO (Laplante voted NO, Delrosario absent).

Page # 1 
MINUTES OF THE SPECIAL MEETING 
OF THE LAWRENCE CITY COUNCIL 
Tuesday, January 6, 2026 
 
A SPECIAL MEETING of the Lawrence City Council was held on Tuesday, January 6, 2026 
The meeting was called to Order at approximately 7:10 p.m. by City Council President, 
Jeovanny Rodriguez. This public meeting of the Lawrence City Council was conducted in 
person at Lawrence City Hall, 200 Common Street and via remote participation. Members of the 
public who attended this meeting were allowed to make comments during the portion of the 
meeting designated for public comment.  
 
He then asked the City Clerk, Eileen Bernal to call the roll:  
Councilor Rosaly Gonzalez [District B] – Present 
Councilor Franklin Miguel [District A] – Present  
Councilor Vivian Marmol [District D] – Present 
Councilor Stephany Infante [District E] – Present 
Councilor Celina Reyes [Councilor at Large] – Present 
Councilor Gregory Delrosario [District C] – Absent 
Councilor Marc Laplante [District F] – Present 
Council Vice President, Ana Levy [Councilor at Large] – Present  
Council President, Jeovanny Rodriguez [Councilor at Large] – Present  
Present - 8. Quorum established.   
 
PUBLIC PARTICIPATION:  
 
The City Council President stated that members of the Public who had signed in for Public 
Participation would be allotted two and a half minutes to speak. He noted that their comments 
should be addressed to the Council as a whole and not to any individual member. Those 
participating were:  
 
H. Maali, 53 Chester Street. Mr. Maali stated that the citizens support the Police Unions. He 
noted that under the impeccable leadership of Chief Aguiler, the Police Department was doing 
well. He also spoke in support of the DPW and the Inspectional Services Department and 
encouraged the city to hire more inspectors. He commended the Public Schools and the 
leadership of Superintendent Ralph Carrero. He praised the Lawrence Teachers and their Union. 
He thanked the Veterans and encouraged the city to hire two new employees in veteran services. 
He encouraged them to activate the council on aging, and to pay the long-term employees as 
much as the new hires. He also spoke in support of Fire Chief Delaney who is doing the best job. 
“Lawrence Always Strong, Always United.”  
 
Richard Russell, 34 Cross Street. Former City Councilor Richard Russell expressed concern 
about the “Blue Light” system of notification for snow emergencies. Specifically, he asked why 
there are not more Blue Lights. Similarly, he wanted the Blue Light alert extended to the City 
Web Page. He also stated that he believes that persons requesting ordinance changes should be 
charged for the publication of the required legal notice in the Eagle Tribune. He similarly 
reminded the Council that the plaques at certain city monuments were supposed to be replaced.
Page # 2 
Specifically, he noted the ones installed in 2023, where the name of the Mayor dwarfed the name 
of the honoree.  
 
The Council President took a point of personal privilege to say thank you to all of the candidates 
who ran for City Council, both the winners and the other candidates. He also specifically thanked 
the winners, noting the time it takes to serve the community, and for putting the city of Lawrence 
first. He acknowledged the two new Councilors and the returning Councilors. He also 
commended the School Committee candidates and the Mayor for their commitment and their 
service.  
 
New Business: 
DOC # 003/26 Authorization to Purchase of Airplane Hanger at Lawrence Municipal 
Airport – John Lavoie, Greater Lawrence Technical School, 
Superintendent of Schools  
The Council President noted that per Rule # 6, all new Documents are sent to Committee, 
however, as a courtesy to Mr. John Lavoie, the Greater Lawrence Technical School 
Superintendent, the President was looking for a Motion to Suspend that Rule to allow discussion 
at the full Council. Councilor Infante made a Motion to Suspend Rule # 6 and it was seconded by 
Councilor Marmol.  
 
After being granted the floor, Councilor Laplante expressed his concern about suspending the 
rules. He stated that while he conceptually agrees with the concept of buying the hanger, he 
believes that there is time and that the Council would be better served sending this Document 
through the normal course of review.  
 
Hearing no further discussion on the Motion, the Council President asked the Clerk for a Roll 
Call vote on the item:  
 
Councilor Marc Laplante [District F] – NO 
Councilor Gregory Delrosario [District C] – Absent 
Councilor Celina Reyes [Councilor at Large] – YES 
Councilor Stephany Infante [District E] – YES 
Councilor Vivian Marmol [District D] – YES 
Councilor Franklin Miguel [District A] – YES 
Councilor Rosaly Gonzalez [District B] – YES 
Council Vice President, Ana Levy [Councilor at Large] – YES 
Council President, Jeovanny Rodriguez [Councilor at Large] – YES 
 
DOC # 003/26 MOTION TO SUSPEND RULE # 6   PASSED  
 
John Lavoie, the Greater Lawrence Technical School (GLTS) Superintendent was present and he 
was invited to come forward and speak on the Document. He noted that the Seller, Bob Davis 
has offers from two other buyers. He was grateful that the Council was considering the matter 
that evening. He also noted that this facility was much better than the hanger currently owned by 
the GLTS as it was larger with plumbing and bathrooms already installed. Similarly, the new
Page # 3 
hanger being considered had A/C and heat, as well as more space for classrooms. He noted that 
running the sewer line alone would be an expense in excess of $300,000. He also noted how rare 
it is for a hanger at the airport to become available. As soon as they purchased this hanger, then 
the GLTS would sell their current hanger.  
 
Mr. Lavoie noted that he had a valuation of $1.2 MIL for the hanger and the purchase price was 
$975,000.  
 
He noted that this would be at no cost to the community as the school would buy the hanger with 
the sale proceeds from their existing hanger and use funds from the schools Excess and 
Deficiency Account.  
 
Mr. Lavoie also noted that he had support from the other GLTS communities.  
 
Mr. Lavoie noted that there is a lot of excitement for the aviation program. That this is the first 
year it will be offered and that 20 students will be accepted into that program in March and over 
100 students have already expressed an interest in the aviation program.  
 
Mr. Octavien Spanner, the Senior Advisor to the Mayor was present and Councilor Infante asked 
if he could come forward to answer some questions. Mr. Spanner confirmed for the Council that 
there are funds available for this purchase. He noted that if the proposed purchase is approved by 
the Council, that the city can afford this, Lawrence has the Free Cash to help and that the city is 
in good financial shape. He noted that Lawrence, while seen as a “poor” community is in the 
financial position to front the funds for this purchase and help the 3 other GLTS communities.  
 
Councilor Marmol, after being granted the floor, noted that while she also believes in following 
the process, she believes that there is an urgency to verify the offer. She also asked Mr. Lavoie 
about any disruptions or challenges to the program as a result of moving from one hanger facility 
to the other. Mr. Lavoie noted that the Students are not physically in the program yet and would 
not be there until the fall of 2026. At that time 10th graders would be starting in the program. Mr. 
Lavoie also noted that their program has the approval of both the Massachusetts Department of 
Education and the FAA.  
 
Councilor Laplante, after being granted the floor, again expressed his concern with the rush to 
get this done. He noted that there is not an MOU in place between the GLTS and the city. He also 
stated that he would like to hear from the airport director on the matter.  
The Airport Manager, Francisco Urena was on-line and joined the meeting via Zoom. He stated 
that at the airports upcoming Commission meeting, scheduled for Thursday, January 15th they 
would be voting to approve the sale to this Buyer/the GLTS. He stated that the Chairwoman of 
the Commission expressed her support for the proposal, but the Commission as a whole had not 
deliberated on the topic yet. He confirmed that this is a 5,000 square foot enhanced facility and 
the fact that it was maintaining an “aviation use” is what the Commission was looking for in a 
purchaser.
Page # 4 
Councilor Laplante again maintained his position that this proposal was not following the normal 
process and he was concerned that the lack of a more thorough review could put the city in a bad 
place.  
Mr. Lavoie noted that any purchase and sale agreement would contain a clause that the purchase 
was contingent upon a favorable vote by the Airport Commission.  
Councilor Infante then made a Motion for the City of Lawrence to purchase a hangar at the 
Lawrence Municipal Airport for $975,000 on behalf of Greater Lawrence Technical School 
(GLTS), with the understanding that GLTS will repurchase the hangar from the City within five 
(5) months for $975,000, plus any additional costs incurred by the City during the holding 
period. Her Motion was seconded by Councilor Marmol.  
After being granted the floor, the Council Vice President Ana Levy, asked if the author of the 
Motion would accept a friendly amendment to allow the Council President to serve as a 
representative of the Council as needed during any negation period. Councilor Infante accepted 
this friendly amendment.  
Councilor Levy also asked if an appraisal was needed. It was noted that the GLTS had a 
valuation but not an appraisal.  
After being granted the floor, councilor Marmol noted that a valuation was not the same thing as 
an appraisal and she wanted to ensure that the property appraised at or above the stated purchase 
price. She asked if the author of the Motion would accept a friendly amendment to make the 
purchase contingent upon a successful appraisal at or above the stated purchase price. Councilor 
Infante accepted this friendly amendment.  
After being granted the floor, the Council Vice President Ana Levy, asked if the author of the 
Motion would accept a friendly amendment to make the purchase contingent upon the approval 
of the Airport Commission. Councilor Infante also accepted this friendly amendment.  
The Clerk was then asked to read the Motion into the record with all three of the amendments.  
The Council President noted that the Council’s next meeting was not until January 20, 2026. The 
GLTS Superintendent wanted to reach out to the Seller to see if he would wait that long. 
RECESS:  
A Motion to Recess was made by Councilor Infante and was seconded by Councilor Marmol. 
The Motion to Recess PASSED by a Unanimous V oice V ote.  
The Council went into a brief recess at 8:05 p.m.  
A Motion to Come Out of Recess was made by Councilor Infante and was seconded by 
Councilor Levy. The Motion to Come Out of Recess PASSED by a Unanimous V oice V ote.  
The Council exited the Recess at 8:14 p.m.
Page # 5 
Mr. John Lavoie let the Council know that he called the Seller during the recess. The Seller was 
not inclined to allow for additional time.  
At that time, hearing no further discussion on the Motion, the council President called the 
question and asked the Clerk to call the Roll:  
Councilor Marc Laplante [District F] – NO 
Councilor Gregory Delrosario [District C] – Absent 
Councilor Celina Reyes [Councilor at Large] – YES 
Councilor Stephany Infante [District E] – YES 
Councilor Vivian Marmol [District D] – YES 
Councilor Franklin Miguel [District A] – YES 
Councilor Rosaly Gonzalez [District B] – YES 
Council Vice President, Ana Levy [Councilor at Large] – YES 
Council President, Jeovanny Rodriguez [Councilor at Large] – YES 
 
DOC # 003/26 MOTION TO APPROVE    PASSED  
 
The Council President then noted that the following Committee meetings would occur on the 
dates and times noted below. He noted that the Committee Assignments would be announced in 
the immediate future and that the Committee would elect their respective chairs and vice chairs 
at their organizational meetings:  
Housing Committee   Monday, January 12th at 6 p.m.  
Budget and Finance Committee Monday, January 12th at 7 p.m.  
Personnel Committee   Tuesday, January 13th at 6 p.m.  
Ordinance Committee   Tuesday, January 13th at 7 p.m.  
As there was no other business before the Council, Councilor Celina Reyes made a Motion to 
Adjourn. Her Motion was seconded by Councilor Infante. There was no discussion on the 
Motion and it PASSED by a Unanimous V oice V ote.  
The Meeting Adjourned at 8:19 p.m.
